sealed: Written and committed before the LIGHT codec, its packet door, its vault or any measuring code existed. The measurement refuses to run if this file differs from the commit that sealed it, and the record names that commit. A claim that fails is kept as failed, on the page, with what was measured.
build: LIGHT EVERYWHERE: one lossless, mutation-gated codec the estate's organs import as their internal language, signed packets checked before anything is decoded, memory and organ-to-organ messages in LIGHT, translation to standard forms only at the edges, and the language-barrier security claim measured rather than asserted.

material.rule: Every git-tracked .json and .md file of at most 256 KB in the local clones of the estate's PUBLIC repositories (origin sjgant80-hub, public in the estate index), excluding vendor/, node_modules/ and anything under a data/img folder, de-duplicated by SHA-256. A file whose last commit is before 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z is TRAIN; on or after it is HELD-OUT. The shared dictionary and every tuning choice may read TRAIN only. HELD-OUT is read for the first time by the measurement.
material.small: An item of at most 2,048 bytes is a SMALL item: the size of an organ-to-organ message.
material.memory: Every file in the Kar memory directory, packed as one vault (private; only the totals are published).
material.feed: The 180,000 payment records of break-it's UCI feed, as one JSON array of {account, period, amount} records.

claims.claim: LIGHT is 15× denser than JSON: the median HELD-OUT item is at least 15 times smaller as LIGHT than as committed.
claims.measure: median over HELD-OUT items of committed bytes / LIGHT bytes
claims.predicted: FAIL: the estate has measured dictionary coding several times (text about 1.05–1.13×, JSON about 2.7×); a context-modelling coder with a shared dictionary should land near 3–6× on these files, not 15×

claims.claim: Lossless: every HELD-OUT item, every memory file and the feed decode back to exactly the bytes that went in.
claims.measure: byte-for-byte comparison of decode(encode(x)) with x for every item

claims.claim: On the median SMALL HELD-OUT item, LIGHT is smaller than both gzip at level 9 and Brotli at quality 11.
claims.measure: per-item sizes from node:zlib on the same bytes; the medians compared
claims.predicted: HOLD: a shared dictionary is what small messages need, and the standard coders bring none of the estate's own

claims.claim: Over the whole HELD-OUT set, the total of LIGHT's per-item sizes is no larger than Brotli quality 11's.
claims.measure: sum of per-item sizes, LIGHT against node:zlib Brotli 11

claims.claim: One thread on this laptop encodes and decodes at 0.5 MB a second or faster, each way, over the HELD-OUT set.
claims.measure: bytes in / wall-clock seconds, encode and decode timed separately

claims.claim: The whole memory directory packs into one LIGHT vault and unpacks to byte-identical files, every one.
claims.measure: unpack the vault to a fresh folder and compare every file's bytes and name

claims.claim: The memory vault is at least 3 times smaller than the files it holds.
claims.measure: sum of file bytes / vault bytes

claims.claim: break-it's nodes share antibodies as signed LIGHT packets: an attack refused by node 0 is then dropped on sight by nodes 1 and 2, which never saw it.
claims.measure: a real three-node mesh, one attack sent to node 0, the same bytes then sent to nodes 1 and 2

claims.claim: A LIGHT share signed by a key that is not pinned, and a pinned peer's share with one byte changed in transit, are each dropped before a byte of their body is decoded.
claims.measure: the receiving node's answer and its decode count

claims.claim: A share as a LIGHT packet is at least 2 times smaller than the same share as today's JSON.
claims.measure: bytes on the wire, same antigens
claims.predicted: HOLD, narrowly: antigens are signed packets whose 64-byte signatures do not compress

claims.claim: Bytes in a language the estate shares with the world (the fixed corpus of SQL, script, shell, path, template, JSON, XML and HTTP inputs in light/barrier.json) sent to a LIGHT door are refused before anything decodes or interprets them, each with a named stage and a reason: 0 decoded.
claims.measure: the door's answer for every corpus entry, and the decoder's call count

claims.claim: Someone who knows LIGHT's format but not the key gets nothing decoded: a well-formed packet signed by an unpinned key, one with its signature zeroed, and one with a single body byte flipped are each refused at the sender or signature stage.
claims.measure: the door's answer and the decoder's call count

claims.claim: LIGHT does not change data: a correctly signed packet carrying each corpus entry as its data decodes to exactly that entry. The language barrier therefore does not remove injection carried as data; only the edge that renders or executes it can.
claims.measure: decoded value compared with the original for every corpus entry
claims.predicted: HOLD (stated so that no page claims the language alone neutralises injection)

claims.claim: At the page's edge, every decoded corpus entry is shown as text and never becomes markup or code.
claims.measure: rendered through the page's own sink; elements and handlers created by the entries counted

claims.claim: The model reads and writes LIGHT: a local model given records as binary LIGHT (base64) answers questions about them correctly.
claims.measure: qwen2.5 on this laptop, the same questions over the same records as JSON and as LIGHT; correct answers counted
claims.predicted: FAIL: a model cannot undo an arithmetic code in its head; binary LIGHT is for machines, and the model-facing edge is a text dialect

claims.claim: The model-facing text dialect (tongue-pack) costs fewer local-model tokens than minified JSON on the median record-shaped HELD-OUT item, and the model answers the same questions from it as from JSON.
claims.measure: qwen2.5 prompt token counts and the same question set
claims.predicted: HOLD on tokens; answers within one of JSON's

claims.claim: Every outside-facing edge built here (the live page and the command line) decodes LIGHT only through the same verify-first door, and the page passes its own gate: a self-only security policy, no inline script or style, every sink escaped.
claims.measure: the page's test and the door's call sites

claims.claim: The mutation gate kills every mutant of the codec, the packet door and the vault, or each survivor carries a written reason.
Full-estate migration: every organ in the estate that stores or exchanges structured records imports the one codec.
claims.measure: a census of all 1,802 repositories in the estate index: which have an internal store or an organ-to-organ channel, which now read and write LIGHT, which belong to other sessions, and where LIGHT does not win
claims.predicted: FAIL as stated for the whole estate in one build: organs held by other sessions (the cards, the game) are theirs to move, and LIGHT is switched on only where it measurably wins. The census says exactly how far it got.
